title: Maximum residue levels for cyflumetofen
summary: EU discusses increasing cyflumetofen MRL on sweet peppers/bell peppers
update: The European Union (EU) is discussing an increase in the existing maximum residue level (MRL) for cyflumetofen on sweet peppers/bell peppers.
what_changing: The EU is discussing an increase in the MRL for cyflumetofen on sweet peppers/bell peppers from the limit of determination (LOD) of 0.01 to 2 mg/kg. (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.)
why: Following an application for a change of MRLs by the producer of cyflumetofen, the European Food Safety Authority ( EFSA 2026 ) concluded that the proposed increase is unlikely to pose a risk to consumers’ health.
timeline: The new MRL for peppers is expected to apply from early 2027.
resources: Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/1164 as regards maximum residue levels for cyantraniliprole, cyflumetofen, deltamethrin, mefentrifluconazole, mepiquat and oxathiapiprolin in or on certain products EFSA (2024) Scientific support for preparing an EU position in the 55th Session of the Codex Committee on Pesticide Residues (CCPR). EFSA Journal, 22(7): e8841. EFSA (2026) Modification of the existing maximum residue level for cyflumetofen in sweet peppers/bell peppers. EFSA Journal, 24(1): e9877.
